svg.title: Split-conformal prediction interval on a 24-hour demand forecast
svg.desc: The last 36 hours of hourly electricity demand in GW (synthetic, seeded daily cycle with noise) end at a vertical NOW line. A seasonal-profile model, the mean of the same hour over the previous 7 days, forecasts the next 24 hours as a heavy line. Around it, a split-conformal 90% interval is drawn as grid-snapped pixel cells, one column per forecast hour, under its exact vector edges: the band is the forecast plus or minus q-hat. To the right, a pixel histogram of 336 calibration residuals |y − ŷ| shares the same vertical scale; q-hat = 1.60 GW, the 304th smallest of the 336 residuals (k = ceil((n+1)(1−α)), α = 0.1), is a horizontal line that meets the band's upper edge, and a dimension bracket shows that the band half-width equals q-hat. The actual next-day demand is a faint dashed line; 22 of 24 hours fall inside the band, shown by a coverage strip under the time axis.
